modern_name: Kaifeng (Yuan Nan-ching / Bianliang Lu), Henan, China
notes: Pelliot, Notes II pp. 789–791 (entry 294, NAMGHIN): 'I have no doubt that Namghin is Nan-ching = K'ai-fêng', the Chin 'Southern Capital' and the official name of Kaifeng from 1272 to 1288. First proposed by Klaproth, revived by Moule (1927) and Charignon. Anqing is Pauthier's reading, followed by Yule (vol. II, note 1 to ch. LXIX) and most editors. Polo names Nan-ching and Saianfu as 'provinces towards the west', north of the Yangzi, off his own route. 'Nanking' for Nanjing dates only from the 15th century; in Polo's time Nanjing was Jiankang Lu (CHGIS hvd_32291). Point = Wikipedia 'Kaifeng'; CHGIS Bianliang Lu (hvd_84025, 1279–1367) lies about 1 km away. Chapter II-11 follows Yule's Anqing and needs revising. The modern name 'Madagascar' comes from Polo's misread form, via Martin Behaim's globe (late 15th c.). The separate 'magadoxo' row is merged here. Chapter III-07 treats the passage as Madagascar mixed with Mogadishu and needs revising. (Read in the Toyo Bunko scan of Pelliot's Notes, 2026-10-22.)
